gen-gf-warnes-gf-farro: Farro reads friendly and compact, its ascenders cut short and every stroke the same weight. Warnes above it is all stretched, spacious bold; shrink that heading and its swagger fades.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-fragment-mono: Fragment Mono lines its letters up like nails on a ruler. Warnes stretches out above in tapering ink strokes, so the loose, bold heading gives the rigid body something to push against.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-geist-mono: Geist Mono reads like code, with fixed-width letters and big gaps between each one. Geist Mono keeps a longer passage steady and structured, while Warnes stays the expressive, widely spaced voice above.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-genos: Tight, modern and a bit brushed, with Genos pressing its glyphs nearly edge to edge. Warnes is best at flat, bold statements; Genos is best at smooth running text.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-hammersmith-one: Rope-round and sturdy, with Hammersmith One keeping its capitals barely taller than its lowercase. Warnes spreads out bold and tapering above, and the rounded sans body anchors it.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-inder: Slim joins on top, low and level below: Warnes uses hairline connections, while Inder keeps capitals and lowercase close in height. Inder's sans text moves smoothly and quietly, so a longer passage stays easy.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-jaldi: Approachable describes Jaldi, whose tall x-height and gaping c stand out even at small sizes under Warnes. A slightly smaller body than you'd guess works fine for this plain sans.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-kdam-thmor-pro: Flat as a sign-painter's stencil, Warnes lays down bold, stretched letters of uniform weight. Kdam Thmor Pro fills its lines with wide bowls, a modern sans that echoes that flatness.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-krona-one: Warnes writes with a pen that never changes pressure or angle, tapering each stroke just short of touching. Krona One has loosely spaced, cast-iron-tall lowercase, so a modest body size is plenty.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-magra: Rope-thin and stretched, Warnes outlines every letter with no thick or thin parts, while Magra feels big-bodied in every lowercase word. Shrink the heading and the plain sans body wins.
